primitives.name: Shrinkage Player Rating
primitives.verbatim_quote: To correct for this, we construct a penalized regression model that identifies the specific offensive and defensive contributions of each player on each possession, and tune the model using L2-regularization method to optimize its predictive power.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{\\beta}_j': 'Estimated player rating coefficient (dimensionless)', 'y_i': 'Observed outcome for possession i (points scored)', 'x_i': 'Vector of covariates for possession i (player indicators, time, etc.)', '\\lambda': 'Regularization parameter (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players' contributions are additive, data is sparse but structured, and outcomes depend linearly on player presence and context.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High variance in small sample sizes leads to overfitting without shrinkage.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian inference maps player ratings to posterior distributions over offensive/defensive contributions using shrinkage priors.

primitives.name: Offense-Defense Separation
primitives.verbatim_quote: ###### **Abstract** The standard plus/minus model for rating NBA players combines the offensive and defensive capabilities of each player into a single metric.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{PM}_{ij}': 'Plus-minus for player i in game j (points)', '\\text{Off}_{ij}': 'Offensive contribution of player i in game j (points)', '\\text{Def}_{ij}': 'Defensive contribution of player i in game j (points)'}
primitives.assumptions: Offensive and defensive impacts are additive and separable within a game.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player substitution frequency increases, additive separation becomes ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: GSE state transition kernel isolates offensive and defensive effects per possession to simulate real-time tactical shifts.

primitives.name: Home Court Advantage
primitives.verbatim_quote: Furthermore, our model captures net home court advantage on offense, and estimate players' contributions in offense and defense.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{HA}_{\\text{off}}': 'Net home court advantage in offense (points)', 'Y_{\\text{home}}, Y_{\\text{away}}': 'Expected points scored under home/away conditions (points)'}
primitives.assumptions: Home advantage is constant across games and additive to player ratings.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inconsistent venue conditions or non-stationary environments invalidate static HA estimates.

layer2.mapping: GSE incorporates HA as a contextual bias in possession-level offensive models to adjust for environmental variance.
layer2.telemetry: Predictive accuracy difference between home/away simulations

primitives.breakdown_regime: When player substitution or team dynamics vary significantly, model assumptions fail.

The core innovation lies in separating offensive and defensive contributions at the possession level, thereby enabling more granular performance evaluation. The use of L2 regularization (shrinkage) mitigates overfitting in high-dimensional, low-sample settings typical in sports analytics. The model accounts for home court advantage and player substitution dynamics, enhancing predictive validity. This approach aligns with modern Bayesian inference paradigms where prior knowledge (e.g., player baseline performance) is combined with observed data to yield robust posterior estimates. The framework supports both descriptive and prescriptive analytics—describing current player value and predicting future outcomes in simulated games. The methodology bridges classical statistical modeling with contemporary machine learning techniques, offering a principled way to quantify uncertainty in sparse data environments.
